**The document doesn't give these numbers.** The TL;DR win-rate plot is Figure 2 (right), but it is included only as an image. The text never states the values at temperature 1.0 for either method.

What the text does say about that plot:

- **Temperature range:** completions were sampled at temperatures from 0.0 to 1.0, and win rates are against the reference summaries in the test set (p. 9).
- **Only exact values given:** DPO wins about 61% at temperature 0.0, and PPO about 57% at temperature 0.0, which is PPO's best temperature (p. 9).
- **PPO at high temperatures:** PPO's performance "can degrade to that of the base GPT-J model at high temperatures." DPO is described as "much more robust to the sampling temperature than PPO" (p. 9). The Figure 2 caption also says DPO is "more robust to changes in the sampling temperature" (p. 7).

The paper does report one number for PPO at temperature 1.0, but it is not from this plot and not against reference summaries. In the human study (Table 2, p. 10), PPO at temperature 1.0 was compared against PPO at temperature 0. Its win rates were 13% with the GPT-4 (S) prompt, 12% with GPT-4 (C), and 17% with human raters. The text calls it the "lowest" performing method in that comparison (p. 10).

To get the exact values at temperature 1.0, you would need to read them off the Figure 2 (right) image.
